title: Western Plaguelands
body: The Western Plaguelands were once the heart of northern Lordaeron, a country of forest and farmland governed from Hearthglen, with the city of Andorhal serving as the granary of the northern provinces. That bounty became the kingdom's undoing. The Cult of the Damned tainted Andorhal's grain and set great cauldrons in the fields of the largest farmsteads, and the plague that followed killed the people and raised them again as Scourge. Now the trees swell with tumorous growths, diseased beasts roam the hills, and the lich Araj the Summoner rules Andorhal while Scholomance festers beneath the island of Caer Darrow. The Scarlet Crusade holds Hearthglen and the lumber mill below it, and cuts down any who will not follow it, innocents included. Against them stand two small footholds: the Alliance at Chillwind Camp in the south and the Forsaken at the Bulwark on the Tirisfal border, each joined by the Argent Dawn, whose officers call both Horde and Alliance their friends in the war on the dead.

title: Chillwind Camp
body: Chillwind Camp lies at the southern edge of the Western Plaguelands, just north of the Alterac Mountains, and it is the last safe ground for Alliance travelers entering the plague lands. Commander Ashlam Valorfist holds it for the Kingdom of Stormwind and its allies, planning the push on Andorhal. His second, High Priestess MacDonnell, directs the war on the plague cauldrons, while Alchemist Arbington studies the poisons they brew. Officers of the Argent Dawn offer their commission to any who will fight the dead, and Flint Shadowmore of SI:7 keeps watch on the Plaguelands for Stormwind. The camp also shelters Weldon Barov, a nobleman locked in a bitter feud with his own brother.

title: Sorrow Hill
body: Sorrow Hill is the great cemetery south of Andorhal, where the city and the country around it buried their dead long before the plague. Those dead do not rest. Skeletal flayers and slavering ghouls rise from the graves to guard the road toward the city's weaker eastern side, skeletal sorcerers stir among the crypts, and a dread figure called Lord Maldazzar is sometimes seen among them. Here stands the monument of Captain Joseph Redpath of Darrowshire. Nearby, the spirit of Marlene Redpath lingers at her old house on the hill, and the banished illusionist Myranda lives within sight of Uther's Tomb.

title: Uther's Tomb
body: Atop Sorrow Hill stands the tomb of Uther the Lightbringer, first paladin and founder of the Order of the Silver Hand, raised by survivors after he fell to his own student, Prince Arthas. Its epitaph declares that Uther lived and died to defend Lordaeron, and that his light is the light of all humanity. High Priest Thel'danis guards the tomb and purges the evil from scourgestones brought to him.

parts.body: New pilgrims have come with a new age. A draenei anchorite at Chillwind Camp, who in his short time on Azeroth has come to hold Uther above all its heroes, seeks to return a holy symbol the Lightbringer lost to his tomb. Not every visitor comes in reverence. A blood knight at the Bulwark, once Uther's pupil, blames him for the fall of Quel'Thalas.

title: Caer Darrow
body: Caer Darrow stands on an island in still, lifeless Darrowmere Lake, an old fortress that became the seat of House Barov. To keep their lands beyond their own lifetimes, the Barovs struck a bargain with Kel'Thuzad, and beneath the keep grew Scholomance, a school of necromancy. A sickness born there swept the town just as it prepared to welcome Uther the Lightbringer, and no one survived. The townsfolk linger as ghosts, guardsmen, bakers and racing children reliving their last ordinary day. A few remember everything, among them the artist Renfray, who haunts the ruins near the shore, and Magistrate Marduke, who seeks the end of the lich Ras Frostwhisper.

title: Ruins of Andorhal
body: Andorhal was the grain distribution center of northern Lordaeron, and that made it the perfect tool for the Cult of the Damned. Plague-tainted grain went out from its granaries to the villages of the north, and the city itself fell soon after. Its broken walls now shelter a Scourge garrison of skeletal acolytes and executioners, ghouls and flesh golems, ruled from the city's heart by the lich Araj the Summoner. Four watchtowers are thought to direct the movements of his troops. In a ruined inn at the northwest corner, the bronze dragon Chromie labors to mend a timeline the Scourge has torn, and the Annals of Darrowshire still lie in the old city hall.

title: Felstone Field
body: Felstone Field lies northwest of Andorhal, a farm where the Scourge raised one of the four great plague cauldrons of the west. Cauldron Lord Bilemaw guards it with skeletons and ghouls, counted among the greenest troops the Scourge has, though no one wise underestimates them. Upstairs in the farmhouse the ghost of Janice Felstone cowers in a corner, still frantic to send off a parcel she packed before the plague came. Between Felstone Field and Dalson's Tears the Scarlet Crusade has pitched a camp with a command tent, and its crusaders strike at the Scourge and at anyone else who comes near.

title: Dalson's Tears
body: Almost due north of Andorhal lies the farm once called Dalson's Orchard, known now as Dalson's Tears. The Scourge raised a plague cauldron in its field under Cauldron Lord Malvinious, and rotting cadavers, blighted zombies and skeletal terrors crowd the rows. The farm keeps smaller horrors of its own. A diary lies open in the house, a lone skeleton wanders the grounds, and the outhouse, locked fast from outside, has its door splintered at the frame by something within that moans and batters to get out. A sturdy cabinet stands locked as well, its front deeply scratched by violent attempts to force it.

parts.body: The diary's last entry tells the family's end. When Harold Dalson turned, his wife dragged him into the only place she could find that would hold him, locked him in and hid the key on herself. She hoped to flee, but for that she needed money, and their valuables were in the cabinet, whose key she believed Harold kept on him. Worn out, she wrote that she would rest on it.
sources: quest 5058 reward text (Mrs. Dalson's Diary)

parts.body: She never left. The wandering skeleton is what remains of Mrs. Dalson, and the outhouse key was still on her bones. Behind the splintered door waited the ghoul that had been Farmer Dalson, trapped for who knows how long and long past saving, the man she had guessed still carried the key to the family's cabinet.

title: The Writhing Haunt
body: Almost due east of Andorhal, close beneath the ruined city walls, a farm has become the Writhing Haunt. Its plague cauldron is guarded by Cauldron Lord Razarch, and rotting and freezing ghouls shamble among fetid zombies in the fields around it. Hidden inside one of the cottages lies Mulgris Deepriver, a tauren druid who came to the Plaguelands to heal what the Scourge had poisoned. He could not save the land alone, and the plague has taken him in turn. Blind and dying, he spends his last breaths asking strangers to grant the diseased wolves and grizzlies of the region a swift and merciful death.

title: Gahrron's Withering
body: Gahrron's Withering, once Gahrron's Quickening, was the farm of Del Gahrron, out toward the eastern border where the Eastern Plaguelands begin. Its plague cauldron is the last and hardest of the four in the west, for the Scourge has set some of its tougher servants to guard it. No ghouls shamble here. Hungering wraiths, wailing deaths and haunting visions drift through the fields around Cauldron Lord Soulwrath. Beside the barn lies a forgotten shield, once carried by Joseph Redpath of Darrowshire.

title: The Weeping Cave
body: The Weeping Cave opens in the hills of the northeast, just west of the Thondroril River that runs along the border of the Eastern Plaguelands. Nothing in it is wholesome. Vile slimes and devouring oozes slither through its tunnels, one of them grown far larger than the rest, rotting behemoths lurk in the damp, and plague lurkers and diseased grizzlies prowl the slopes about its mouth. No record that survived the plague tells how it came by its name.

title: Northridge Lumber Camp
body: South of Hearthglen, west of the road that climbs up to the town, stands the Northridge Lumber Mill. Before the last great war it was run by the Dumah family and worked by families such as the Levines, but when war came the Dumahs fled to Stormwind, and the Scarlet Crusade has since taken the mill for itself. Scarlet lumberjacks now cut timber for the Crusade's work in Hearthglen, while diseased wolves and carrion lurkers prowl the edges of the clearing. The mill's old owners have not forgotten it. Nathaniel Dumah has come back as far as Chillwind Camp, and Mickey Levine, whose family once worked here, plots its ruin from the Bulwark.

title: Hearthglen
body: Hearthglen was once the seat of government for these lands, and when the plague first struck it held out against the Scourge. Today it is the Scarlet Crusade's stronghold in the west. Scarlet workers labor to rebuild the town while paladins, sentinels, magi and priests keep its streets, and Huntsman Radley and Cavalier Durgen lead the forces along Hearthglen Pass below. Atop the guard tower by the gates the Crusade keeps the Mark of the Lightbringer, a holy relic of Uther. Some in the Alliance believe the town holds more than historical importance, and Stormwind's scouts have come to count the Crusade's strength.

title: Mardenholde Keep
body: Mardenholde Keep rises over Hearthglen, the old seat from which the lords of Mardenholde governed these lands. In better days it was a center of trade and commerce, and diplomats of the Alliance often passed through its halls. When Lordaeron fell, the Scarlet Crusade claimed the keep as its headquarters in the region, and its zealots now keep watch over the town below while its workers rebuild it. Today the keep's halls belong to Highlord Taelan Fordring, who waits within for reinforcements from Tyr's Hand.

title: Araj the Summoner
body: Araj the Summoner is the lich who rules Andorhal for the Scourge. Once master of Scholomance, he left the school on Caer Darrow to claim the ruined city as his own, and from its heart he oversees the plague cauldrons poisoning the farms around it. A formidable retinue of guardians attends him, and the garrison filling the old streets stands between him and his foes, so both Commander Valorfist and High Executor Derrington know it will take many allies to reach him. Both demand the same proof of his end: a shard of his phylactery.

parts.body: Araj can be brought down, though a lich is not so easily ended. When his guardians are broken and his body destroyed, his phylactery remains where he fell, and from it the shard his enemies demand can be taken as proof that the lord of Andorhal was overthrown.

title: Commander Ashlam Valorfist
body: Commander Ashlam Valorfist leads Chillwind Camp, posted there by Stormwind and its allies to hold back the rising tide of the Scourge. He is a methodical soldier. Finding Andorhal's western and northern roads too strongly held, he plans to strike through Sorrow Hill and the weaker eastern road, to mark the city's watchtowers with beacon torches, and at last to bring down Araj the Summoner. He trusts the cauldron campaign to High Priestess MacDonnell and the Scholomance key to Alchemist Arbington, and he means to turn the scourgestones that High Priest Thel'danis cleanses into Holy Mightstones, to bathe the Scourge in righteous fire. Success he rewards loudly, in Stormwind's name.

title: Highlord Taelan Fordring
body: Taelan Fordring is Highlord of the Scarlet Crusade in Hearthglen and master of Mardenholde Keep, the town's old seat of government. He rules the Crusade's stronghold in the west, where Scarlet workers rebuild the town under the eyes of paladins, sentinels, magi and priests. His crusaders attack outsiders on sight, and his officers Huntsman Radley and Cavalier Durgen hold the pass below the town, while the Highlord himself waits in the keep for reinforcements from Tyr's Hand.

parts.body: The Highlord carries a name heavier than his rank. He is the son of Tirion Fordring, though after Tirion's exile his mother told the boy that his father had died, and he grew up believing it. Taelan became a paladin of the Silver Hand and fought the Scourge until the order was shattered, then found a place in the Scarlet Crusade and rose to become its Highlord.

title: Chromie
body: Chromie is the name the bronze dragon Chronormu takes among mortals, and she wears the form of a small, cheerful gnome, choosing not to drown in the sorrow of the places she is charged to watch. She has made her home in the ruined inn of Andorhal, in a room unlike the rest of the city, for she works from another timeline so as not to contaminate this one. Someone, most likely the Scourge, has tampered with Andorhal's past: temporal parasites infest the silos, and watches lie with their hands frozen at the moment the plague struck. Andorhal is not the only sorrow she watches, for the old tragedy of Darrowshire has caught her eye as well.
sources: npc_text 3584, 3585 (Chronormu, bronze dragonflight, choice of visual demeanor, sentry of sorrowful places)
quests 4971, 4972 descriptions and texts

title: Myranda the Hag
body: Myranda the Hag was once a master illusionist of Lordaeron. In better days she was a trusted advisor at Mardenholde Keep, until she openly dissented from a verdict of the Order of the Silver Hand and was banished for her insolence. Now she lives near Uther's Tomb on Sorrow Hill and warns passers-by to walk lightly. Her old loyalties endure, and she still weaves illusions and guises for those she trusts, though her craft fades with time and distance. Her friends are not all of one side, and she has aided the Horde before.

parts.body: To one who came bearing Tirion's gifts, Myranda told the rest. It was Tirion Fordring she had served, his most trusted advisor in his days as Lord of Mardenholde, and his was the verdict she had spoken against. She had known this day would come, and she agreed to weave the illusion that would carry his gifts into Hearthglen.
sources: quest 5861 completion text (I knew this day would come) and reward text (Tirion's most trusted advisor when he held rank as Lord of Mardenholde; dissented the verdict; banished)
quest 5862 description (an illusion to allow entry into Hearthglen); RewardNextQuest of 5861, QuestType 2, Flags 0, started by Myranda 11872

parts.body: To the Horde she is an old friend. Handed a letter left blank on purpose, she read in it the intentions of its maker and smiled, asking how Rexxar fared. She owes the Warchief a favor or two, she said, and so she agreed to weave an illusion that could fool the black dragonflight.

title: Alexi and Weldon Barov
body: Alexi and Weldon Barov are the last heirs of House Barov, whose holdings once took in Caer Darrow, Brill, Tarren Mill and Southshore. Alexi stayed when the family gave itself to the Scourge and is now undead. Weldon fled during the war and remains human, a cowardice his brother despises, while Weldon curses himself for once sparing Alexi's life. The deeds to the family fortune lie somewhere in Scholomance, and each brother wants them found before the other can claim them. Alexi lounges under Horde protection at the Bulwark, Weldon under Alliance guard at Chillwind Camp.

parts.body: With the deeds recovered, the brother who holds them sees one obstacle left: the other. No rival heir may live to contest the fortune, so he pays for his brother's head, to be taken from under the guard of the opposing camp by whatever means the hired blade sees fit.
sources: quests 5342, 5344 descriptions (slay him, return his head; under Alliance protection at Chillwind Camp, under Horde protection at the Bulwark)

parts.body: The head was brought back, and the surviving brother crowed over it. House Barov had one heir now, he gloated, and its fortune was secure and his alone, and he sent the hired killer away with a purse and a parting insult.
sources: quests 5342, 5344 reward texts (only I hold the power and fortune; my fortune secure; keep the change, leave my sight)

title: Eva Sarkhoff
body: Eva Sarkhoff and her husband Lucien served House Barov at Caer Darrow, she as head maid. When the Barovs gave themselves to the Scourge, their servants became subjects for the experiments of Doctor Theolen Krastinov, the Butcher, and the Sarkhoffs died in his hands. Their spirits linger on the island. Eva greets strangers with the courtesy of an old household, then asks that the Butcher be found within Scholomance and destroyed, and that their remains be burned to ash, for he is responsible for the deaths of thousands.

parts.body: With the Butcher destroyed and their remains burned, Eva felt her spirit begin to heal, but the work was not done. Krastinov served a dark master, Kirtonos the Herald, who still lives, and it is said that Jandice Barov stewards the blood of innocents from the Butcher to him.
sources: quest 5382 reward text (my spirit healing; more to be done)
quest 5515 description (Krastinov's master Kirtonos still lives; Jandice Barov stewards the blood of innocents)

parts.body: Summoned by the blood of innocents, Kirtonos came and was destroyed, and with his death, Eva said, a chapter of the horrible tale of Scholomance came to a close. In thanks the Sarkhoffs gave a piece of their own essence, which lets its bearer speak with the other lost souls of Caer Darrow.
sources: quest 5384 description and reward text

title: Marlene Redpath
body: Marlene Redpath is a wandering spirit who haunts her old house on the hill south of Andorhal. So many died at the battle of Darrowshire, she says, and worse befell others. When the battle began she hid her young niece, Pamela, and she has never learned what became of the girl, though her heart still longs to know. Darrowshire lies to the east, beyond Gahrron's Withering. Among the graves of Sorrow Hill below stands the monument of Captain Joseph Redpath of Darrowshire, who bore her family's name.
sources: quest 5142 description (so many died, and worse; hid her niece Pamela; Darrowshire to the east beyond Gahrron's Withering)
quest 5152 (house on a hill south of Andorhal)

Also dropped that Pamela is Joseph's daughter (EPL's 13928 part 3, QUEST_DONE 5152). The opening is now what her own quest 5142 tells. No parts: her quests are EPL's. It is where the quest flow tells them, before EPL's Annals (DONE 5154) tell how he was corrupted.

parts.body: Marlene wishes her brother Joseph could be with his daughter again, but she knows it cannot be. The Scourge twisted his soul and made him a monster, and his body was trampled and destroyed years ago. Yet his wedding ring still lies beneath his monument on Sorrow Hill, and she hopes that Chromie, a strange gnome of very strange powers in the ruined inn of Andorhal, might somehow change his fate.

title: Janice Felstone
body: Janice Felstone did not escape the plague. Her ghost cowers in an upstairs corner of the Felstone farmhouse, only half aware of the living, murmuring that time is running out for her and for everyone. She is frantic to send off a parcel before it is too late. She meant to ride out with it, she says, and it should still be by her horse, though where that is, and where the parcel was bound, she cannot make clear.

parts.body: The parcel waits in the barn, dusty and overlooked among the ruin. It is addressed in a hurried hand to her family, and its delivery was due more than four years ago. Whether the one it was meant for outlived the plague the farm cannot say, but the census keepers of the cities may know.
sources: quest 5021 reward text (package in the barn)
quests 5022, 5023 descriptions (hurried hand; over four years late; the Stormwind and Undercity censuses)

parts.body: The name on the parcel, read closely, is Emma Felstone of Stormwind. Whether she is even alive no one at the farm can say, but Stormwind's City Hall keeps records of the people of the city, and the Royal Factors of its census may know where she can be found.
sources: quest 5022 description (addressed to an Emma Felstone of Stormwind; Stormwind City Hall records, Royal Factors of the Stormwind Census); Alliance only (AllowableRaces 1101), started from the parcel 175894 in this zone, unused by any zone file

parts.body: The parcel reached her family at last. It held her personal effects, among them the deed to the farm, which her kin chose not to reclaim, and half of a good luck charm; her husband had held the other half. The half-charm was sent back in the hope it would let her rest, but the ghost only looked up and asked her John where he had put his half, for they cannot be together without both.
sources: quest 5050 description (personal effects, deed, half charm, husband had the other half)
quest 5050 reward text and 5051 description

parts.body: John's half was found on the farm and the charm made whole. The moment she grasped it her shimmering form changed, and she looked out with clear, sad eyes. She was free, she said, and needed the charm no more, and she pressed it on the one who had freed her, in the hope it would bring them the solace it had brought her.

title: Mulgris Deepriver
body: Mulgris Deepriver is a tauren druid who came alone to the Plaguelands, hoping to heal the damage the Scourge had done to nature. There was little one druid could do. He tried to cure the suffering animals until the plague took him as well, and he now lies blind and dying in a cottage at the Writhing Haunt. He asks any who will listen, whatever their race, to put aside their differences and grant the diseased wolves and grizzlies a swift and merciful death.

parts.body: When the grizzlies had been put down, Mulgris had one thing more to give. Sensing his end, he had written what he had learned of the plague into a glyphed oaken branch, meant for his friends in the Cenarion Circle. The creatures of this land could rest now, he said, and so would he, and with a last sigh he lay still on the cottage floor.
sources: quest 4985 request and reward texts (vision faded; the branch; his death)
quests 4986, 4987 descriptions (Cenarion Circle)

parts.body: The branch, warm to the touch, carried within it the place it was meant to go, and it reached the Cenarion Circle. In its glyphs the druids found a great store of lore about the plague the Scourge spreads across the land, and they promised that his work would not be wasted.

title: The Scourge Cauldrons
body: Eight great cauldrons stand in the lands of old Lordaeron, four in the west and four in the east, pouring the Scourge's plague into the air. The necromantic might of Kel'Thuzad is too strong for anyone to simply shut them down, so the defenders of Chillwind Camp and the Bulwark mean to subvert them instead, changing the plague they brew into something that harms the Scourge. Under High Priestess MacDonnell and Shadow Priestess Vandis, champions are to strike at the western cauldrons one by one: Felstone Field with its greener troops first, then Dalson's Tears, the Writhing Haunt, and at last Gahrron's Withering and its wraiths. Each cauldron lord is thought to carry a key, and from each vessel a sample must be drawn for Alchemist Arbington and Apothecary Dithers to study.

parts.body: The first cauldron gave way. Bilemaw's key opened the access panel at Felstone Field, and a sample of the poisons swirling inside was drawn off. From it a counter agent can be brewed and pumped back into the air to weaken the Scourge. It will be an ongoing ordeal, for the cauldrons must be struck again and again, but kept up, it could give the living a great advantage when battle comes.
sources: quests 5216, 5229 reward texts (Bilemaw's key, access panel, spigot)
quests 5217, 5230 reward texts (counter agent, ongoing ordeal, advantage in battle)

parts.body: In time the last cauldron, at Gahrron's Withering, was opened too. With samples from all four, the counter agents can be poured in through four separate vessels, and the Scourge will be hard pressed to keep its enemies out of all of them, even with Kel'Thuzad behind it. The work will never truly end, but the plague can now be turned against its makers.
sources: quests 5226, 5236 request and reward texts (last cauldron, four separate vessels)

title: The Road to Andorhal
body: Both Chillwind Camp and the Bulwark have their eyes on Andorhal. Commander Valorfist finds the city's western and northern roads too well fortified and means to come at it from the east, sending his first recruits to thin the undead buffer on Sorrow Hill. High Executor Derrington faces a second enemy first: a Scarlet Crusade camp between Felstone Field and Dalson's Tears, which he means to answer by burning its command tent and planting a Scourge banner, so the Crusade will take its vengeance on the dead. Beyond lies the city itself, its four watchtowers thought to direct the Scourge's movements, and at its heart the lich Araj the Summoner.

parts.body: With the first blows struck, both commanders sent agents into the ruins with beacon torches, magical devices that mark targets for their troops. Planted in the doorway of each watchtower, the beacons now send back strong signals from all four. The towers are marked as the first targets of the attack, and the preparations for an open fight for the city are in place.
sources: quests 5097, 5098 descriptions, request and reward texts

parts.body: The final target was the lich at the city's heart. Reaching him through his retinue of guardians took many allies, but Araj the Summoner was defeated at last, and the shard of his phylactery carried home was hailed as the proof of a victory for the ages.
sources: quests 105, 211 descriptions and reward texts

title: The Key to Scholomance
body: Scholomance on Caer Darrow is barred by a door no one can pass without a key. Alchemist Arbington at Chillwind Camp and Apothecary Dithers at the Bulwark have each studied the school and reached the same answer: a Skeleton Key. Its outer layer must be built from the fragments of many skeletons, gathered in and around Andorhal, and hardened with the strongest metal within a suitable mold. Last, the key needs a signet of power from one who can naturally open the way into the school.

parts.body: Once the fragments are tempered for the forge, only a mold remains, and it can come only from Krinkle Goodsteel, a goblin smith in Gadgetzan who has made molds for such macabre things before. He works for the highest bidder and charges in advance, and it is the champion, not the key's maker, who must pay his fee.
sources: quests 5537, 964 reward texts (temper; goblin blacksmith in Tanaris, highest bidder)
quests 5538, 5514 descriptions and texts (Krinkle Goodsteel, fee up front)

parts.body: Once the stem was forged in the lava atop Fire Plume Ridge, only the signet remained, and it could belong to one being alone: Araj the Summoner, the school's former master, who rules Andorhal. His scarab, seized from his fallen phylactery, must be mounted as the head of the key.
sources: quests 5801, 5802 descriptions and reward texts (Fire Plume Ridge; Araj)
quests 5803, 5804 descriptions (former leader of Scholomance, scarab from his fallen phylactery)

parts.body: With a special solvent the scarab was fused on as the head of the key, infusing it with the power to breach the locked door, and the Skeleton Key was finished at last. Whether it truly opens Scholomance, its maker admits, there is only one way to be absolutely sure.
sources: quests 5803, 5804 reward texts (solvent, scarab as the head of the key)

title: The Mark of the Lightbringer
body: When Uther the Lightbringer died, a holy symbol of his faith was lost, and the Scarlet Crusade is said to keep it atop their guard tower by the gates of Hearthglen. Two very different visitors want it. Anchorite Truuen, a draenei at Chillwind Camp who has studied Azeroth's heroes in his short time on the world and holds Uther above them all, wishes to return it to his tomb in tribute. Mehlar Dawnblade, a blood knight at the Bulwark who once studied under Uther, blames his old teacher's handling of Prince Arthas for the ruin of Quel'Thalas, and wants the relic for his revenge.

parts.body: With the mark recovered, the anchorite set out for the tomb, and the Scourge, drawn by the relic's purity, fell on them along the way. At the tomb the ghost of Uther himself appeared, touched that anyone would go to such lengths in his memory. He bade the anchorite's companion rise and granted a blessing, a sign that heroes long gone might rise again in each of the living.
sources: quest 9446 description and reward text
creature_text 17238 groups 3 to 7, 17233 groups 0 to 2

parts.body: Mehlar laced the mark with fel magic, to be used before Uther's statue to defile the tomb. The Lightbringer's ghost answered instead. He saw his former student's hand in it, grieved that his heart had turned so dark, and sent back word that he forgave him and hoped he would turn to restoring Quel'Thalas. Mehlar raged at the forgiveness and drove his agent from his sight.
sources: quest 9444 description and reward text

title: A Plague Upon Thee
body: The Scarlet Crusade holds the Northridge Lumber Mill, and two people who remember it before the war want it taken away from them. At Chillwind Camp, Nathaniel Dumah, whose father ran the mill until the family fled to Stormwind, has tried and failed to rout the Crusade by force. At the Bulwark, Mickey Levine, whose family worked the mill and lost their livelihoods and their lives, has sworn never to rest until the zealots are gone. Both settle on the same weapon: termites from the mounds of Plaguewood near Stratholme, a breed that survived the plague and the Scourge alike, gathered by the hundred.

parts.body: The termites were packed into a steel reinforced barrel and carried to the mill, where it was set high atop a crate at the heart of the timbers, the insects already restless inside. A crowbar found nearby pried it open, and the swarm was loosed to make the mill useless to the Crusade, while the one who freed them prayed to get out before the termites found them too.
sources: quests 5902, 5904 descriptions and reward texts (steel reinforced barrel, atop a crate, restless)
quests 6389, 6390 descriptions and reward texts (crowbar, release)

parts.body: For Nathaniel Dumah it was more than sabotage. With the mill lost to the Crusade, he laughed, his father's spirit could rest at last, and he himself could live in peace, for the zealots never had any right to the mill.
sources: quest 6389 reward text
